Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  August 1, 2024

The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council
Chambers located on the ninth floor of City Hall on August 1, 2024. Commissioner Denmon
called the meeting to order at 6:01 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Cynthia McLemore - District
  3, Christopher Beck - District 4, Henry Brown - Commissioner at
  Large
  Absent  Commissioner Octavio Padilla - District 2

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Teresa Estrada  Recreation Superintendent
  Juan Mata  Park Supervisor
  Geoffrey Okamoto  Human Services Program Manager of Transit
  Operations
  Stephanie Maldonado  Senior Management Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None

MINUTES. None

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORTS - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. Park Supervisor, Juan Mata reported the following:
Graffiti Division - Staff has been working extensively in District 4, focusing on the
Crenshaw, Century, Imperial, and Prairie corridors, as well as the surrounding residential
areas. Other efforts include repainting and water blasting city poles in front of the Intuit
Arena to restore them to their original state. Additionally, Vincent Park has been tagged
which we are addressing as part of our ongoing maintenance efforts. The Graffiti hotline
is (310) 412-8739. Parks Division - Staff planted trees at Edward Vincent Park to celebrate
Juneteenth. We are currently seeking bids for janitorial services for all of the outdoor park
restrooms. Several water leaks were repaired at Darby and Edward Vincent Parks. Fields,
bleachers, and backstops were prepped at Rogers Park for the Inglewood Little League All-
Star Tournament and the Tournament of Champions. Inglewood’s 50/70 and Juniors teams
won both tournaments.

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

REPORTS - RECREATION. Recreation Superintendent Teresa Estrada reported the
following: Summer Recap - Only one (1) week left of Summer Camp. Between Rogers,
Darby, and Siminski (Kiddie Camp) Parks, over 600+ kids were served. Camps were filled
the first week of signups. All swimming pool classes filled up quickly as well, serving 400
participants. Movies in the Park - The last movie will be held on August 17 at North Park
after Councilman Padilla’s Cook Off. We have had 300+ residents in attendance for the
previous dates leading up to our final event. Pre-activities before the movies have been
successful with live interactions before each event. Early Learners Program - Open House
will be held on August 17 from 10:30 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. for all sites. For more information
on our Inglewood Youth Sports Leagues, visit our city sports website at
https://cityofinglewood.leagueapps.com/

REPORTS - HUMAN SERVICES. Human Services Program Manager for Transit Operations,
Geoffrey Okamoto reported the following: Senior Nutrition - We are serving
approximately 450 seniors per week through home delivered meals for homebound
seniors and congregate meals at our Senior Center. We continue to provide fresh produce
weekly in collaboration with the Social Justice Learning Institute, and monthly shelf stable
meal boxes in collaboration with the Los Angeles Food Bank. Transportation - Our
paratransit program continues to provide trips to seniors and the disabled community in
Inglewood and Hawthorne. We recently promoted our last part time bus operator to a full
time status to add more driver resources for the service. We are also looking to hire an
additional part-time bus operator to help eliminate any service gaps that may arise in the
future. Senior Center Operations - July saw some amazing activities, trips and events,
including our July 4th celebration with hot dogs, games and prizes, as well as our trip to
watch the Los Angeles Dodgers play against the San Francisco Giants. Our Senior Center
continues to thrive with a plethora of activities and special events coming up. Our
highlights for August include trips to Venice and Redondo beaches. We are also proud to
continue our collaboration with the Los Angeles County Aging & Disabilities Department
to provide free tablets for our seniors. Our distribution date is tomorrow, August 2. Child
and Adult Care Food Program/Summer Food Service Program - The Summer Food Service
Program is operating at six (6) different locations for youth 18 and under. The sites are
Ashwood Park, Crenshaw Library, Darby Park, Siminski Park, Rogers Park, and Edward
Vincent Jr. Park. We be provide breakfast, lunch, and snacks at different sites, and service
times vary according by site.

REPORTS - DIRECTOR. None

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner Beck thanked staff for the District 4 Concert
at Park, said it was a good event and had a great turn out. He and his son frequently visit

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

Darby Park and asked how we can add more activities and classes for seniors. Teresa
Estrada recently had a meeting with the Recreation Supervisor to discuss more
programming for seniors while we are currently seeking instructors. Commissioner
Denmon complimented Darby Park’s parking lot, with the addition of the new cement
blockers in parking stalls. He also mentioned District 1 would be hosting a picnic at Darby
Park on August 24 with tons of activities, food, bands and dance team at 1:00 p.m. to 6:00
p.m.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the
meeting adjourned at the hour of 6:34 p.m.
